87:
The study "Design Research Approach in Developing Technology-Mediated Learning Modules in Practical Mathematics for Technical Vocational Education" addresses the lack of tailored online learning technologies for technical-vocational students in the Philippine K to 12 curriculum, specifically for subjects like Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW). Using the design research model by McKenney and Reeves (2013), researchers employed an iterative methodology to develop and validate design principles for mathematics modules.

The research involved two iterations. The first iteration involved twelve Grade 11 students using modules on unit conversions, algebraic expressions, and ratios/percentages. Following feedback, modules were refined for a second iteration involving twelve Grade 12 students. Findings identified students as ICT-proficient learners who face socio-economic and connectivity challenges. Effective design principles included using small-group collaborative learning through synchronous and asynchronous discussions centered on simplified, authentic, problem-based tasks. Teachers were most effective when acting as facilitators, mentors, and course designers. Facebook was found to be the most effective technology due to its accessibility for messaging and file sharing. Successful module presentation utilized a multimedia approach, including video tutorials, clear text, and practical exercises.

Statistical analysis showed the second iteration group achieved significantly higher mean scores, moving evaluations from "good" to "excellent." The study concludes that technology-mediated modules developed through design research effectively facilitate learning for technical-vocational students.
